destination.name: Corsica and Sardinia
destination.pitch: Two islands with the best mountain-to-sea range in the Mediterranean, joined by a 50 minute ferry that decides the whole shape of your ten days.

because.nature: Granite peaks over 2,500 m, glacial lakes, a red-rock marine reserve and water as clear as anywhere in the Mediterranean, all within a day of each other.
because.exploration: Two islands, two languages, one ferry hinge and interior roads that make every 60 km a two hour project.
because.food: Corsican charcuterie and brocciu in the hills, Sardinian pane carasau, porceddu and Vermentino on the other side of the strait.
because.relaxation: Rondinara, Capriccioli and Le Bombarde are as good as beaches get in Europe, if you go in June or September.
because.culture: Genoese citadels, Paoli's short-lived republic in Corte, Catalan-speaking Alghero and Bronze Age nuraghi nobody else in Europe has.
because.adventure: GR20 stages, the Restonica lakes, a guided scramble to Cala Coticcio and the 654-step Escala del Cabirol.
because.city: There is no city here worth the name; Bastia and Alghero are towns for a night and a dinner.

destination.caveat: Corsican rental cars cannot be taken on the Sardinia ferry, so you walk on at Bonifacio and hire a second car at Santa Teresa, and in August both islands are full, expensive and slow on the roads. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Bastia
cities.base: Vieux Port or Terra Nova citadel, the two halves of old Bastia; you fly in here and it is the only sane start for Cap Corse and Patrimonio.

cities.name: Calvi
cities.base: Inside or just below the citadel for the quay and the evening; the Pinède beach hotels are cheaper but you walk 20 minutes to dinner.

cities.name: Corte
cities.base: Anywhere along Cours Paoli or below the citadel; the town is small and the point is being 35 minutes from the Restonica shuttle and 5 minutes from the Tavignano trailhead.

cities.name: Restonica valley
cities.base: No beds beyond the Tuani campsite; the road above the Pont de Tragone has been closed to cars since the November 2023 storms and hikes now start at the A Frasseta shuttle stop.

cities.name: Bonifacio
cities.base: Haute Ville for the cliffs and quiet after the day boats leave; the marina is louder and pricier in July and August.

cities.name: Col de Bavella
cities.base: A pass at 1,218 m with a couple of refuges and gites but no proper hotel; you come for the day from Bonifacio or Porto-Vecchio.

cities.name: Palau
cities.base: Palau itself, near the port: 30 minutes from the Santa Teresa ferry, 15 minutes by boat to La Maddalena and 40 minutes to the Costa Smeralda beaches without paying Porto Cervo prices.

cities.name: La Maddalena and Caprera
cities.base: The town has hotels but Caprera, the beaches and Cala Coticcio are a day from Palau by the 15 minute ferry; sleeping here adds nothing but a second ferry queue.

cities.name: Alghero
cities.base: The walled old town: everything is within ten minutes on foot and you drive out to Capo Caccia, the nuraghi and Bosa.

cities.name: Capo Caccia
cities.base: A headland with a car park, a bar and the Neptune's Grotto staircase; nowhere to sleep, 30 minutes from Alghero.

outings.name: Lac de Melo from A Frasseta
outings.why: Since the 2023 storms the Restonica road is closed above the Pont de Tragone, so the walk to the lake now starts at 900 m at the shuttle terminus, not at Grotelle, and is a real 6 to 7 hour round trip on rough ground.
outings.season: May to September (shuttle dates); snow above Grotelle into J
outings.fallback: Walk from A Frasseta to the Grotelle bergeries and back, about 5 hours, with the river pools on the way down

outings.name: Gorges du Tavignano to the Passerelle de Rossolinu
outings.why: Starts on foot from the top of Corte with no shuttle or car park, follows a mule path above the gorge to a footbridge and swimming pools; exposed and hot after 11:00 in summer.
outings.fallback: Turn around at the first pools after 45 minutes

outings.name: Cascade des Anglais from Vizzavona by the train
outings.why: The mountain railway from Corte to Vizzavona takes 45 minutes, then a shaded 40 minute walk on the GR20 to a chain of granite pools; the easy day and the wet-weather day.
outings.season: Year round; pools cold before July
outings.fallback: Coffee at the Vizzavona station and the short loop to the Cascade only

outings.name: GR20 stage 1 taster: Calenzana to Bocca di u Saltu
outings.why: The first day of the GR20 climbs 1,300 m from Calenzana to the Ortu di u Piobbu refuge on unshaded granite; going up to the Bocca di u Saltu pass and back gives the feel without the refuge night, and it is still hard.
outings.season: June to early October; storms most July afternoons
outings.fallback: Cirque de Bonifatu loop from the Auberge de la Forêt, 3 hours in shade

outings.name: Scandola and Girolata by boat
outings.why: The only way into the Scandola marine reserve is by boat; red porphyry cliffs, ospreys and a lunch stop at roadless Girolata, cancelled in any swell and sold out days ahead in August.
outings.fallback: Drive to Notre-Dame de la Serra and walk the Revellata peninsula

outings.name: Cap Corse loop: Erbalunga, Centuri, Nonza, Patrimonio
outings.why: A 110 km circuit on a road that never straightens, with fishing harbours on the east, the black beach at Nonza on the west and Patrimonio wine on the way home; do it clockwise so the sea is on your side.
outings.fallback: Erbalunga and back for lunch, 2 hours

outings.name: The Lavezzi islands boat
outings.why: A 30 minute shuttle from the marina to a granite archipelago with no shade, no shop and the clearest water in Corsica; take the first boat, take water, and leave before the midday crowd lands.
outings.fallback: The one hour cliffs and grottoes boat, which runs in weather the Lavezzi boat will not

outings.name: Capo Pertusato from the Haute Ville
outings.why: The clifftop path east from the citadel to the lighthouse looks back at the whole town hanging over the sea; no shade, so it is a morning walk or an evening one.
outings.season: Year round; closed on high fire-risk days in summer
outings.fallback: Walk to the Saint-Roch belvedere and back, 40 minutes

outings.name: Trou de la Bombe at Bavella
outings.why: Two hours of switchbacks each way from Bonifacio to the Col de Bavella, then a 3 hour loop under the granite needles to a hole in the ridge; the drive is the hard part and the pass is 15 C cooler than the coast.
outings.fallback: Cascade de Piscia di Gallu from the Ospedale road, 1.5 hours, halfway there

outings.name: Cala Coticcio with the guide
outings.why: Since 2023 the cove on Caprera is capped at 60 people a day in five hour slots and you can only go with a park-licensed guide booked at least three days ahead; a rough 45 minute descent each way, and worth it.
outings.fallback: Cala Spalmatore or the Relitto beach on Caprera, no booking

outings.name: La Maddalena and Caprera by car
outings.why: Drive onto the 15 minute ferry, loop the panoramic road on La Maddalena, cross the causeway to Garibaldi's house and the Caprera beaches; in August the ferry queue back can be an hour.
outings.season: Year round; beaches June to September
outings.fallback: Walk on as a foot passenger and stay in La Maddalena town

outings.name: Capo Testa and the Valle della Luna
outings.why: Wind-carved granite headland beside the ferry port, with a valley of boulders that has had a hippy camp in it since the 1970s; good the morning you land from Corsica or the evening before you sail.
outings.fallback: Rena Bianca beach in Santa Teresa

outings.name: Costa Smeralda beach day: Principe and Capriccioli
outings.why: Two of the best coves on the Aga Khan's coast, no cap yet but the Principe car park costs 12 euros a day and is full by 09:30 in July and August; go before 09:00 or after 16:00.
outings.fallback: Cannigione town beach, 15 minutes from Palau

outings.name: Neptune's Grotto by the Escala del Cabirol
outings.why: 654 steps cut into the Capo Caccia cliff down to the cave mouth and 654 back up; entry is 18 euros with a timed slot, and the cave shuts when the sea is up.
outings.season: Year round; boat access April to October only
outings.fallback: Nuraghe Palmavera and Le Bombarde beach

outings.name: Bosa by the coast road
outings.why: The SP49 runs 45 km along empty cliffs with griffon vultures overhead to a pastel river town with a Malaspina castle and Malvasia wine; slow driving, nowhere to stop for lunch until Bosa.
outings.fallback: Drive as far as the Torre Argentina turnoff and back

outings.name: La Pelosa at Stintino
outings.why: The famous shallow turquoise beach is capped at 1,500 people a day from June to September, booked online for 3.50 euros with a mandatory mat under your towel; one hour each way from Alghero and it still fills.
outings.season: June to September (booking); shoulder months free
outings.fallback: Lazzaretto beach at Porto Conte, 15 minutes from Alghero

places.name: Vieux Port
places.note: The horseshoe harbour under the citadel is where Bastia actually lives at 19:00; the terraces are fine, the fish is better a street back.

places.name: Église Saint-Jean-Baptiste
places.note: The twin towers you see from every angle of the port; the baroque interior is bigger and gaudier than the town deserves, and free.

places.name: Musée de Bastia
places.note: Genoese governors' palace with a good hour on how Corsica went from Genoa to France; open daily in July and August, closed Sunday and Monday and over lunch from October to April.

places.name: Marché de Bastia, Place du Marché
places.note: Saturday and Sunday mornings only: brocciu, figatellu, lonzu and canistrelli from the producers, which is what you came to Corsica to eat.

places.name: U Paisanu
places.note: Half deli, half table: charcuterie boards, pastizzu and figatelli with no reservation, the honest cheap lunch in Bastia.

places.name: Col Tempo
places.note: Market cooking on a monthly menu, a few tables, and the dinner I would book for the one Bastia night; check the day off, it changes.

places.name: Cap Corse Mattei boutique
places.note: The 1872 shop for the island's quinine aperitif, on the big square; buy a bottle here and drink it on ice all week.

places.name: Erbalunga
places.note: Fishing village on a rock with a ruined Genoese tower, 20 minutes up the cape; the first stop on the Cap Corse loop and the right one for lunch.

places.name: Nonza and the black beach
places.note: A village on a 100 m cliff over a grey-black beach made of asbestos mine tailings; walk up to the Paoline tower for the view, swim somewhere else.

places.name: Domaine Orenga de Gaffory, Patrimonio
places.note: The best-known Patrimonio estate, with Niellucciu reds and a Muscat you will not get at home; the tasting room doubles as a contemporary art gallery.

places.name: Citadelle de Calvi
places.note: Genoese walls on a rock with the whole bay and the Cinto massif behind; free to walk, and the ramparts at sunset beat any paid thing in town.

places.name: Quai Landry
places.note: The yacht quay is where Calvi drinks; overpriced, loud in August, and still the place for the first evening beer looking at the citadel.

places.name: Plage de Calvi, La Pinède
places.note: Four km of sand under pines, shallow and calm, walkable from the old town; sunbeds are 20 euros but the free sand is the same sand.

places.name: Pointe de la Revellata
places.note: Track out to the lighthouse on the peninsula that closes the bay, with rock coves to swim from; no shade, so go before 10:00.

places.name: Notre-Dame de la Serra
places.note: A chapel on a knoll with the classic postcard view of Calvi, the bay and the mountains; ten minutes by car, best in the last light.

places.name: Sant'Antonino
places.note: A 9th century village coiled round a granite peak, all stone stairs and vaulted passages; park below and walk up, and combine with Pigna.

places.name: Pigna
places.note: Blue-shuttered craft village that revived Corsican polyphony; luthiers, a music box maker and summer concerts in the auditorium, small and quick.

places.name: Clos Culombu, Lumio
places.note: The serious Calvi appellation estate, Vermentinu whites and Niellucciu reds tasted in the cellar; ring ahead outside July and August.

places.name: A Candella
places.note: Terrace on the citadel walls facing the sea, Corsican veal and brocciu cannelloni; book a rampart table, the inside ones lose the point.

places.name: U Fanale
places.note: Family Corsican cooking on the road out towards the Revellata, wild boar stew and fiadone; a 20 minute walk or a short taxi, worth it to escape the quay.

places.name: Chez Tao
places.note: Piano bar in the citadel founded by a White Russian in 1935, cocktails at 18 euros and a terrace over the bay; summer only, and skip the food.

places.name: Citadelle de Corte and the Belvédère
places.note: The eagle's nest fort above the two gorges, with the free belvedere at the end of the rock giving the view down the Tavignano; ten minutes up from Cours Paoli.

places.name: Musée de la Corse
places.note: Ethnography of shepherds, chestnuts and the vendetta inside the citadel; 5.50 euros, daily May to October, closed Sunday and Monday and at 17:00 the rest of the year.

places.name: Cours Paoli and Place Gaffori
places.note: The one street of the town Paoli made capital of his 1755 republic, with a university, bullet holes still in the Gaffori house and coffee at 2 euros.

places.name: Corte Friday market
places.note: Friday mornings only, and the place to buy the interior's coppa, lonzu and brocciu from the people who made it; buy the hike lunch here.

places.name: Restonica shuttle from Corte station to A Frasseta
places.note: May to September the valley above Tuani is closed to cars and this 4 euro return bus, booked on the Via Corsica app before you leave town because there is no signal up there, is the only way to the Melo trailhead.

places.name: Restonica river pools below Tuani
places.note: The part of the valley you can still drive to: granite basins of cold clear water off the road, full of Corte families on hot afternoons, free.

places.name: Gorges du Tavignano path
places.note: The gorge nobody drives to: a mule path from the top of town to the Rossolinu footbridge and pools, 2 hours each way, no shuttle and no car needed.

places.name: U Trinighellu to Vizzavona
places.note: The narrow-gauge train south over the Vecchio viaduct to the forest station at Vizzavona, then the easy GR20 walk to the Cascade des Anglais pools; four trains a day, check the return time before you set off.

places.name: A Casa di l'Orsu
places.note: Corsican mountain cooking done properly: charcuterie board, veal with olives, chestnut flour desserts; small, so book, and closed out of season.

places.name: U Museu
places.note: The terrace on the ramp under the citadel is the reason to come; brocciu omelette and wild boar are dependable, the service in August is not.

places.name: Haute Ville and the Bastion de l'Étendard
places.note: The medieval town on top of the limestone cliff, houses overhanging 70 m of air; the streets are free, the bastion charges 3.50 euros, and after 18:00 the day boats have gone.

places.name: Escalier du Roi d'Aragon
places.note: 187 steps cut diagonally down the cliff face to sea level, 3.50 euros, closed in high wind and from November to March; go first thing before the queue forms.

places.name: Cimetière marin and Saint-François
places.neighborhood: Bosco, west end of the Haute Ville
places.note: The white mausoleum town at the tip of the plateau, quiet even in August, with Sardinia on the horizon 12 km away; free and the best sunset in Bonifacio.

places.name: Cliffs and grottoes boat, SPMB
places.note: The 70 minute loop under the citadel to the Sdragonato cave and the Grain de Sable, 26 euros, every half hour; the only way to see the town from below, and the sea is calmest before noon.

places.name: Îles Lavezzi shuttle
places.note: Granite islets with Caribbean water and zero shade or shops, 37 euros return, boats every hour in summer; the 09:00 boat gets you two hours before it gets crowded.

places.name: Sentier du Capo Pertusato
places.note: The clifftop path from the Saint-Roch belvedere to the lighthouse and the cove below it, 4.5 km each way with the town behind you the whole time; no shade at all.

places.name: Plage de Rondinara
places.neighborhood: 20 km north, off the Porto-Vecchio road
places.note: A near-closed shell of a bay with water like a pool; parking is 6 euros and the last 3 km of road are single track, so it is full by 11:00 in August.

places.name: Plage de Palombaggia
places.note: The most photographed beach in Corsica and, in July and August, the most crowded, with 40 euro sunbeds and an hour to park; Rondinara is closer and better on the same day.

places.name: Sartène
places.note: Mérimée's 'most Corsican of Corsican towns', grey granite and no view of the sea; come for the charcuterie shops on the Place Porta and pair it with Filitosa, 30 minutes further.

places.name: Filitosa
places.note: Bronze Age statue-menhirs with carved faces and swords standing under olive trees, the best prehistoric site in Corsica; about 9 euros, and a 90 minute drive from Bonifacio.

places.name: Trou de la Bombe, Aiguilles de Bavella
places.note: Three hour loop from the pass through pines to a 9 m hole punched through a granite ridge; the two hour mountain drive each way from Bonifacio is the real cost of the day.

places.name: Kissing Pigs
places.note: Wine bar under hams hanging from the ceiling, charcuterie and cheese boards and Corsican wines by the glass; no bookings, so go at 19:00 or wait.

places.name: Stella d'Oro
places.note: Old family place in the upper town doing aubergines à la bonifacienne and fish from the strait since 1960; more expensive than it looks, and worth one dinner.

places.name: Bonifacio to Santa Teresa ferry
places.neighborhood: Santa Teresa Gallura port, 30 km west
places.note: 50 minutes across the Strait of Bonifacio on Moby or Ichnusa Lines, 15 to 44 euros a head by season with 2 to 7 sailings a day; walk on, because Corsican hire cars are not allowed across, and collect the Sardinian car in Santa Teresa.

places.name: Capo Testa and the Valle della Luna
places.note: Granite boulders sculpted by the wind on a headland beside the ferry port, with a nudist-and-hippy valley on the far side; the natural first or last stop in Sardinia.

places.name: Roccia dell'Orso
places.note: A bear-shaped rock that Homer may or may not have meant, 3 euros and a 15 minute climb from the car park, April to early November; the view over the archipelago is the point, not the bear.

places.name: Palau to La Maddalena ferry
places.note: Delcomar and Maddalena Lines every 15 to 30 minutes, 15 minutes across, about 5 euros a passenger and 12 to 16 for a car each way; no booking, but the August queue back to Palau runs late.

places.name: Cala Coticcio with a park guide
places.note: 60 people a day in five hour slots, park fee 3 euros plus a licensed guide booked three days ahead through lamaddalenapark.it; the rough 45 minute descent is why it still looks like this.

places.name: Compendio Garibaldino, Caprera
places.note: The white farmhouse where Garibaldi retired and is buried, kept as he left it; 7 euros, closed Mondays, a good hour between two Caprera beaches.

places.name: Spiaggia del Principe
places.note: The Aga Khan's favourite cove, still no cap or booking but 12 euros a day to park and a 15 minute rocky path down; arrive before 09:00 or accept towels touching.

places.name: Spiaggia di Capriccioli
places.note: Two small sand coves split by granite with juniper down to the water, paid parking and a 5 minute walk; less famous than the Principe next door and easier for an afternoon.

places.name: Porto Cervo Piazzetta
places.note: A 1960s resort village built to look old, with 20 euro spritzes and a marina of superyachts; look at it for half an hour on the way back from the beach, do not eat here.

places.name: San Pantaleo Thursday market
places.note: Thursday only: a granite village under the Monte Cugnana teeth fills its piazza with pecorino, ceramics and linen; more craft than food, and the cafe on the square is the thing.

places.name: Cantina Surrau
places.neighborhood: Arzachena, on the Porto Cervo road
places.note: Glass-and-granite winery with Vermentino di Gallura DOCG and Cannonau tastings from about 20 euros; the one Costa Smeralda stop that is about Sardinia rather than money.

places.name: Ristorante Da Robertino
places.note: The old-school Palau seafood house: spaghetti with bottarga, grilled catch by weight, and a lobster fregola that needs ordering ahead; book in summer.

places.name: Agriturismo Sardo da Paolina
places.note: Fixed Gallurese menu on a farm: pane carasau, antipasti of their own cured meats and cheeses, zuppa gallurese, then porceddu off the spit, with house Vermentino; dinner only, booked, and you will not finish it.

places.name: Bastioni Marco Polo
places.note: The Catalan sea walls with bars along the top and Capo Caccia across the bay; the sun sets straight into the sea here, so the whole town walks it at 20:00.

places.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria and the campanile
places.note: A Catalan Gothic bell tower on a church rebuilt so often it has three styles; the tower climb is a few euros and the only high view over the roofs, hours are short and seasonal.

places.name: Mercato Civico
places.neighborhood: Via Sassari, edge of the old town
places.note: The covered market for pecorino, bottarga, pane carasau and the morning's fish; closed Sundays, dead after 13:00, and where to assemble a beach lunch.

places.name: Grotta di Nettuno
places.note: A sea cave with a lake and columns at the foot of a 110 m cliff, 18 euros with a timed slot, reached by the 654-step Escala del Cabirol or a boat from the port; shut whenever the sea is rough, so check the morning of.

places.name: Nuraghe Palmavera
places.note: A 3,500 year old Bronze Age tower village with a meeting hut and 50 round houses, 7 euros, free parking, on the way to Capo Caccia; the thing Sardinia has that nowhere else does.

places.name: Tenute Sella & Mosca
places.note: A 19th century estate with 500 hectares of vines, a wine museum and tastings of Torbato and the Anghelu Ruju dessert red; tours in summer, shop and tasting year round, closed Sundays.

places.name: Spiaggia Le Bombarde
places.note: The Alghero locals' beach, pine-backed sand with clear water and a paid car park; busy at weekends but nothing like the Costa Smeralda, and no booking.

places.name: Punta Giglio
places.note: A 2 hour loop through macchia to WW2 gun batteries on a 100 m headland facing Capo Caccia; free, empty, and the walk to do the day the grotto is shut.

places.name: Bosa
places.neighborhood: 45 km south by the coast road
places.note: Pastel houses stacked under a Malaspina castle on the only navigable river in Sardinia, with Malvasia to taste; the empty coast road from Alghero is the reason to go, so leave time for it.

places.name: Al Tuguri
places.note: 24 seats in a 16th century house, Catalan-Sardinian cooking over an open fire since 1978; now only Friday and Saturday dinner and Sunday lunch, so book the week before.

places.name: Trattoria Lo Romani
places.note: The inland Sardinia table in a fish town: maccarrones de busa, culurgiones and porceddu when they have it, closed Mondays; the safer bet for a first Sardinian dinner.

places.name: Bar Focacceria Milese
places.note: Focaccia stuffed with Sardinian salumi and pecorino for 6 euros at a counter by the port, closed Tuesdays; the lunch before the beach.

places.name: Agriturismo Sa Mandra
places.note: The famous farm dinner near Alghero: eight courses of their own cheeses, cured meats, ravioli and porceddu carved at the table for about 50 euros; touristy now but the pig is still right, and you need a taxi.
